title: Karkadeh (Sudanese hibiscus tea)
steps: Rinse the hibiscus flowers and put them in a pot with the water and ginger.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove from heat, add the sugar, and stir until dissolved.
Strain, cool, and chill for several hours.
Serve over ice with lemon.

title: Lugaimat (Sudanese fried dough balls in syrup)
steps: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar and salt with the warm water to a thick, sticky batter, and rest for 1 hour until bubbly.
For the syrup, boil the sugar and water for 8 minutes with lemon juice, then add the vanilla and cool.
Heat the oil to 170 C.
Drop in balls of batter using two spoons and fry for 3 to 4 minutes until golden.
Drain, dip in the syrup or pour it over, and serve warm.

title: Mullah tagalia (Sudanese red minced beef sauce)
steps: Fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, and spices and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the mince, breaking it up, and fry until browned.
Pour in the water, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until thick and the oil rises to the surface.
Season and serve with bread, rice or asida.

title: Sudanese basbousa (semolina cake with syrup)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and grease a baking tin.
Mix the semolina, coconut, sugar and baking powder, then stir in the yoghurt, butter and vanilla.
Rest for 15 minutes, then spread in the tin and cut into diamonds, pressing an almond on each.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden.
Meanwhile boil the syrup ingredients for 10 minutes and cool.
Pour the cold syrup over the hot cake, rest, and serve.

title: Tamiya (Sudanese falafel)
steps: Drain the soaked chickpeas and blend them in a food processor with the onion, garlic, herbs and spices to a coarse, grainy paste.
Rest the mixture for 30 minutes, then stir in the bicarbonate of soda.
Form into small patties or balls.
Heat the oil to 180 C and fry in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden brown.
Drain on paper and serve in bread with salad and tahini.
